profile_note: email | review-only | assistant. email: no Slack, the EA drafts and holds and never sends, briefings go to the board and ~/.ea/state/reports/. review-only: email without drafting. assistant: Slack, channels, buttons, the resident and plugins. Set by /setup; read by scripts/install/setup.sh, run-agent.sh, the shells and ea-doctor.
_doc: Operational configuration for the EA system. Controls master pause, eval toggles, log level, quiet hours and travel mode. Missing file = every key below at its default. Keys starting with '_' are stripped by preprocessor/ea_config.py load(); the *_note keys are ignored by the reader and kept as inline documentation.
ea_enabled_note: Master switch. When false, all cron agents (morning-briefing, afternoon-catchup, weekly-audit, scheduling-check, priority-check) exit immediately. The Slack bot stays running but responds with a paused status instead of invoking Claude. Background maintenance (token refresh, ledger sync, scheduled sends) continues regardless.
eval_postcommit_enabled_note: Not read by the post-commit hook: this file is the resident's to write, so the hook takes its switch for the unit tests and prompt-only evals from EA_POSTCOMMIT_TESTS in the committer's environment or eval_postcommit_enabled in the owner's private evals.json (tests/evals/eval_gates.py). The nightly full-mode evals and the weekly release tests are not set here: they run a model as the owner, so their switches are eval_full_enabled and release_tests_enabled in the owner's private evals.json (tests/evals/eval_gates.py).
log_level_note: Controls log verbosity across components. Valid: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR. The EA_DEBUG env var overrides this to DEBUG. Bot restart needed for log level changes (happens automatically on each commit via post-commit hook).
quiet_hours_note: Timezone-aware quiet hours (preprocessor/quiet_hours.py). Proactive Slack posts that would land inside the local window are held and flushed as one digest when the window ends. The window is read in the ACTIVE timezone: travel_mode.timezone while travelling, else the home timezone from scheduling-preferences.json. allow_urgent lets sentinel-class alerts through the hold. only_when_traveling=true engages the hold ONLY while travel mode is active, so at home the 4am briefing still fires on time; set it false to also hold overnight at home. ea_config.get_quiet_hours() re-defaults every missing subkey, so a partial block here is safe.
travel_mode_note: While enabled and on/before `until` (YYYY-MM-DD), the active timezone for quiet-hours math becomes `timezone` (an IANA name, e.g. 'America/Anchorage') instead of the home tz. It auto-reverts after `until` with no rewrite needed, so a stale block is harmless. Normally written by the set-travel flow rather than by hand. ea_config.get_travel_mode() re-defaults every missing subkey.
_not_read_by_ea_config: mail_mediation lives in THIS file but is read by preprocessor/mail_mediation.py, not ea_config.py, so it is deliberately absent from this template. Never let a template copy overwrite the live value: on the deployed host it gates whether ea-bot can send mail at all. Merge this template into the live file key-by-key, never replace it.
models_note: Per-lane model overrides read by the Slack bot (ea_config.get_models()). room_specialist: the persistent session each #ea-<project> room runs on, pinned when the room's session is minted. The resident's model is EA_RESIDENT_MODEL, the per-thread default is EA_MODEL, the cron agents choose per agent in run-agent.sh. Email and letter bodies are written by the email-author subagent (.claude/agents/email-author.md), which carries its own model.
efforts_note: Per-lane effort levels (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) read by ea_config.get_efforts() and passed as --effort beside the lane's model, so a model change never changes effort silently (the CLI's default effort differs by model). room_specialist is the default a new room's session is minted with; a room pins its own effort with `python3 preprocessor/ea_channels.py set-effort --channel <id|name> --effort <level>` (for example xhigh for a room that needs it). Empty means the CLI default for that model.
rooms_note: rotate_bytes: a project room's session starts fresh once its transcript passes this many bytes; the new session starts from the project pack and the room's recent history.
update_note: Automatic updates (scripts/update.py, docs/updates.md). channel: auto (latest on the assistant profile, stable on email and review-only), latest (every signed release from main), stable (the release the maintainer marked stable) or off. An hourly owner job installs a newer signed release when the bot and the cron lanes are idle, and switches back when it does not come up healthy. ~/.ea-private/update.json ({"channel": "off"}) outranks this value, since this file is the EA user's to write. An install whose code tree the post-commit hook writes, and that has no update key, is left to the hook.
routing_note: Model routing (preprocessor/model_routing.py, docs/llm-lanes.md section 1.1): which model does each task. local is the owner's own endpoint in remote-llm.json, hosted is Claude, auto keeps the remote-LLM switches and the tiers block as they are. review (the still-open check, the nightly reconcile, the scheduling backstop) is hosted only: the stakes floor. mail and tagging take hosted only while the keep list is empty: the keep floor. Owner processes read only ~/.ea-private/routing.json, which the web chat's Settings screen and `model_routing.py set` write; this copy shapes what the EA shows, since this file is the EA user's to write.
backends_note: Where mail, calendars and other people's free/busy come from (ea_config.get_backends; docs/macos-native-accounts.md). mail.backend: graph (Outlook through Microsoft Graph, with any Gmail accounts beside it), gmail, or macos (the accounts in the Mac's Internet Accounts, through Mail.app; no app registration). calendar.backend: graph (Outlook plus the Google accounts in scheduling-preferences.json), google, or macos (every calendar EventKit sees). availability.provider, a choice apart from both: graph (Graph getSchedule on a registration's token), owa (the same call on the outlook-web-auth plugin's token) or none (no colleague's calendar is read; the solver offers times and the invitees pick). The recommended Mac setting is macos, macos and owa. On a Mac the owner-private native-accounts.json, which also names the accounts, mailboxes and calendars the EA sees, outranks these values for owner processes.
room_reply_check_note: Project rooms only. After a turn, a reply that states an item's status with no ledger or mail read behind it, or that says something does not exist, goes back to its own session once with the sentences to verify; the second pass returns the reply to post. Each bounce is logged to ~/.ea/logs/reply-check.jsonl. false switches the pass off.
chat_note: Chat platform (ea_config.get_chat()): frontend is slack, zulip, web or memory (tests only). The web block configures the bot's own web chat (docs/webchat.md): the loopback bind and port, the path under which it serves, the public URL the owner opens, the Tailscale login that counts as the owner (trust_tailscale_header false turns that sign-in off), the pairing token file and store (empty: beside the store, in the owner-private directory), and backfill_days, the days of history a shadow web chat copies in when the bot starts (0: none). The zulip block names the server site, the bot's email, the owner's Zulip user id and the private streams (stream for the EA channel, sched_stream optional, dm_stream standing in for the DM); notify maps each notifier channel key to a stream and topic. The Zulip API key is ZULIP_API_KEY in .env.secrets, never here. get_chat() re-defaults every missing subkey, so a partial block is safe.
